item.title: Madang police gearing up for 51st Independence celebrations
item.description: Madang police are prepared for the province's two- day 51st Independence celebrations from 15th to 16th September. Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim said policing arrangements have been activated across all six districts to ensure the celebrations are conducted in a safe, peaceful, and well- managed manner.
item.content:encoded:
Madang police are prepared for the province's two- day 51st Independence celebrations from 15th to 16th September.

Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim said policing arrangements have been activated across all six districts to ensure the celebrations are conducted in a safe, peaceful, and well- managed manner.

The PPC has instructed all police personnel to remain highly vigilant before, during, and after all official programs and community activities connected to the independence festivities.

He also said that members of the public can expect increased police presence in key areas, including main event venues, town centres, transport routes, and other locations where big crowds are expected.

Superintendent Baim emphasized, "Police will strictly deal with anyone who attempts to disrupt the celebrations or undermines public safety."

He warned that those who intend to cause trouble will face consequences under the law.

“We will not tolerate anyone trying to disrupt the celebrations. You will be severely dealt with according to law,” Baim said.

He further reminded the people of Madang that Independence is not only about celebration but also about meaningful reflection and renewed commitment.

"This important national milestone should encourage a positive transformation in attitudes and behavior—moving from negative practices to constructive actions that strengthen both communities and the nation.

“Independence is a time for a shift in our mindsets—change attitudes from bad to good. Think of what little things we can do for the development of the province and the country,” the PPC said.

He added that citizens must also understand that development requires support from everyone—not only institutions and leaders.

Baim urged residents to play their part by maintaining a good mindset, respecting one another, and avoiding actions that can create disorder during the Independence period.

“If you don’t want to be part of development for Madang, you better pack up and go home. There could be better things for you to do at home than just staying in urban areas without a good mind frame,” he said.

In addition to maintaining peace and order, Madang police is also reminding small craft owners and boat operators to take seriously the advice and warnings issued by the national weather service during periods of adverse weather.

People are urged to avoid unnecessary travel and to follow official guidance for safety.

PPC Baim stressed that police rescue capacity can be limited during dangerous weather conditions. He therefore urged all concerned parties to prioritize safety over schedules and journeys.

“All small craft owners must take heed of the warning from the National Weather Service. Stop travelling in bad weather conditions.

"Police can’t go into bad weather to rescue you. We are human beings just like you, with very limited resources—so be very mindful of that,” said PPC Baim.

He further encouraged cooperation among community members, including friends and families who may urge others to travel despite warnings.

According to PPC Baim, the safest decision during storms or hazardous weather is to stay ashore until conditions improve.

Baim is calling on all residents, event participants, and visitors to celebrate responsibly.

The command also urged people to observe lawful conduct at all times, avoid disturbances, and respect public peace.

"I also urge communities to refrain from harmful behaviour such as vandalism, fighting, and any acts that could threaten lives and properties.

“People of Madang must celebrate in colours without any interference,” Baim said.

Meanwhile, the special Independence police operation will be launched on Monday.

item.title: Infant amongst survivors of Madang boating incident
item.description: An infant and an eleven-year-old boy were amongst survivors of a boating incident between Raikos and Madang on Friday, police confirmed. Provincial Police Commander for Madang, Superintendent Robert Baim revealed that a motorised dinghy carrying 18 people, including the operator, departed Saidor Station at 7am yesterday and was three hours into the trip when they encountered rough seas at Tabalip
item.content:encoded:
An infant and an eleven-year-old boy were amongst survivors of a boating incident between Raikos and Madang on Friday, police confirmed.

Provincial Police Commander for Madang, Superintendent Robert Baim revealed that a motorised dinghy carrying 18 people, including the operator, departed Saidor Station at 7am yesterday and was three hours into the trip when they encountered rough seas at Tabalip Point, 18 nautical miles south of Madang Town.

All 18 persons were thrown into the sea when the boat capsized.

"They were adrift for about five years or until 3pm when a passing vessel that was travelling to Raikos spotted them and rescued 10 of them. They were immediately taken to the provincial hospital for medical assessment.

"A second search and rescue operation was subsequently conducted, during which a further five survivors were located and rescued, brining the total number of survivors rescued or located to 15 persons out of the original 18 persons on board," PPC Baim said.

According to medical officers at Modilon Hospital, the survivors who were assessed were generally in good condition, with no serious injuries or medical conditions reported.

Some survivors experienced general fatigue and tiredness and were medically cleared.

Superintendent Baim added that three persons remain unaccounted for.

They include 1 male adult, 1 adult female; and another 11-year-old boy.

The three missing persons are believed to have entered the water wearing yellow life jackets and reportedly swam in the direction of the Bilbil area.

Police have notified Ileg Police Outpost and requested assistance in alerting coastal communities in the Bugati area and the wider Astrolabe Bay region to remain vigilant and immediately report any sighting or information concerning the missing persons.

Superintendent Baim said the incident highlights the serious dangers posed by unsafe marine travel, particularly when vessels are operated beyond their safe capacity or when operators fail to properly assess sea and weather conditions.

“The safety of passengers and crew must remain the highest priority whenever travelling by sea.

"Overloading a dinghy or small craft can make the vessel unstable and significantly increase the risk of an accident, particularly in rough weather or challenging sea conditions,” Baim added.

Baim, meanwhile; has also directed Water Police to begin fully enforcing the Small Crafts Act and its regulations, warning that operators who disregard marine safety requirements will face the full force of the law.

He said continued incidents are concerning because awareness programs have been repeatedly conducted amongst coastal communities and marine operators.

“Despite repeated awareness programs, we continue to see incidences that can be avoided if operators and passengers strictly comply with safety requirements. Everyone using small crafts must take responsibility for their own safety and the safety of others,” he stated.

Dinghy operators and skippers are reminded to,

Passengers are also encouraged to speak up if they believe a vessel is dangerously overloaded or being operated in an unsafe manner.

Superintendent Baim warned that persons who disobey the Small Crafts Act and its regulations may face enforcement action, including arrest and legal proceedings where applicable.

“Skippers have a responsibility to operate their vessels safely and within their approved passenger capacity. Carrying more passengers than a vessel can safely accommodate puts lives at unnecessary risk,” he said.

The Madang Provincial Police Command is also urging coastal communities in the Saidor, Bugati, Bilbil and wider Astrolabe Bay areas to remain alert and immediately notify Police, maritime responders or other relevant authorities if they see or receive information about the three missing persons.

He said police will continue working with relevant authorities, maritime responders, and coastal communities to support search and rescue efforts, promote responsible marine transport, and strengthen compliance with marine safety requirements throughout the province.

PPC Baim's message to the people of Madang is to protect lives, comply with the law, and travel safely.

item.title: New Zealand and Madang PHA launch climate- resilience health care project
item.description: Three major health facilities in Madang Province are now proud recipients of new and improved healthcare facilities under the Building Community- Level Climate Resilience (BCCR) project. The project is a partnership supported by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and implemented by the Fred Hollows Foundation of Papua New Guinea, the Madang Provincial Health Authority and the F
item.content:encoded:
Three major health facilities in Madang Province are now proud recipients of new and improved healthcare facilities under the Building Community- Level Climate Resilience (BCCR) project.

The project is a partnership supported by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and implemented by the Fred Hollows Foundation of Papua New Guinea, the Madang Provincial Health Authority and the Foundation for People and Community Development, a local non- government organisation in Madang.

The beneficiaries of the project, which had cost K2 million, are Saussi Health Centre, which is run by the Evangelical Brotherhood Church (EBC), Usino Health Centre, and Yagaum Rural Hospital, run by the Lutheran Church.

Saussi and Usino are in the Usino/ Bundi District whilst Yagaum is in Madang District.

The project was officially launched on Thursday by New Zealand's High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea, Her Excellency, Georgina Roberts, and Dr Martin Daimen, Chief Executive Officer of the Madang Provincial Health Authority.

The joint launching for the three health centres was conducted at Yagaum, witnessed also by officers from Saussi and Usino.

Her Excellency Roberts said the Madang project was one of the projects built on the long- standing partnership between New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

"This relationship started way before Independence," she said.

She added that the partnership, whether in eyecare, rural health, or any other services, would not have been possible without the people's support.

"All of you made this possible, Madang PHA, National Department of Health, Provincial Government, National Government, and the management of the three health centres. I would like to congratulate all of us who were involved in this project," Her Excellency Roberts said.

Speaking in Tok Pisin, she emphasised, "Yumi mas wok Bung wantaim." (we must work together).

The NZ High Commissioner added, "It's a great privilege during my very first visit to Madang to be able to officiate at this launching. I've been in PNG for only six months now."

She urged people in the local catchment areas that will benefit from the project to continue to advocate for good health, adding the project is a testament of the commitment that the people of New Zealand have towards Papua New Guinea.

Key upgrades across the three pilot health care facilities included solar power systems with battery storage capacity of upbto 36 KVA at each facility, ensuring reliable electricity for health care services, and essential medical equipment, installation of six 9, 000 litre water tanks, three 5, 000 litre water tanks, overhead tank stands, water pumps, gutters and downpipes, improving access to safe and reliable water supply.

She said additional upgrades included six ceiling fans, 12 air-conditioning units, handwashing stations, patients and visitors ablution facilities, verandah extensions, disability access ramps, paving, window repairs with mesh wire, roofing improvements, broader building infrastructure rehabilitation works with paintings and fencing.

Her Excellency Roberts further stated that the B- C- C- R project demonstrates how national and Provincial Health Authorities, local communities, and N- G - O partners can work collaboratively to deliver climate- resilience and environmentally sustainable upgrades to rural health facilities.

Meanwhile, Madang PHA CEO, Dr Martin Daimen, described Thursday's launching as more than just a ceremony.

He said, "Today is a celebration of a deep, enduring and respectful partnership between the governments of New Zealand and Papua New Guinea, through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and Fred Hollows Foundation (FHF). New Zealand has always been a trusted partner. New Zealand has proven that true development is built on neutral respect and local capacity building."

item.title: Central music, arts and culture festival start in Bereina
item.description: The Central Music, Arts and Culture Festival has officially commenced in Bereina, Kairuku district, bringing together musicians, artists, cultural groups and communities from across Central Province. The three-day festival which commenced yesterday and ends on Sunday, is showcasing the province’s rich cultural heritage through music and traditional performances.
item.content:encoded:
The Central Music, Arts and Culture Festival has officially commenced in Bereina, Kairuku district, bringing together musicians, artists, cultural groups and communities from across Central Province.

The three-day festival which commenced yesterday and ends on Sunday, is showcasing the province’s rich cultural heritage through music and traditional performances.

The event is also providing an opportunity for local artists, farmers, small businesses and entrepreneurs to promote their talents, products and services.

Governor for Central Rufina in officially opening the festival said, the event is more than a celebration of music and dance, but an expression of the province’s identity and history.

“This festival is not just music and dance. It is memory. It is identity. It is the drumbeat of our ancestors speaking to us today,” Governor Peter said.

She said the songs, dances, arts and traditions of Central’s diverse communities carry stories and history that must be preserved for future generations..

She said the colours, songs and traditions showcased at the festival are what make Central Province unique.

The Governor also encouraged Central people to remain proud of their cultural identity and use it to create opportunities for the province.

She said the festival demonstrates the potential of cultural and adventure tourism, with Central Province’s diverse cultures, coastline, rivers, forests and highlands offering experiences for visitors.

“This is adventure tourism. This is cultural tourism. This is Central province tourism,” she said.

Governor Peter said the festival is the second major cultural festival hosted by her government, following the event held in Kwikila, Rigo District in 2024.

She said such events are intended to unite Central communities, protect the province’s identity and demonstrate the economic potential of local communities.

The festival also forms part of the province’s broader effort to promote its cultural heritage while creating opportunities for local businesses and the creative sector.

Governor Peter urged the people of Central to carry their heritage forward and pass it on to their children.

“We will stay united, proud and strong. We will carry the heritage of our ancestors and hand it to our children unbroken,” she said.

The Central Music, Arts and Culture Festival continues in Bereina throughout the weekend, with cultural performances, music, arts and community activities.

item.title: Kokoda Junior High hosts 3rd annual provincial cultural show
item.description: Seven schools from across Northern Province came together this week for the 3rd annual Provincial Schools Cultural Show, held at Kokoda Junior High School to promote language, culture, and peace among students. Held under the theme “Celebrating Our Culture, Shaping Our Future”, the one-day event was funded by United Nations, Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization or UNESCO PNG in collab
item.content:encoded:
Seven schools from across Northern Province came together this week for the 3rd annual Provincial Schools Cultural Show, held at Kokoda Junior High School to promote language, culture, and peace among students.

Held under the theme “Celebrating Our Culture, Shaping Our Future”, the one-day event was funded by United Nations, Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization or UNESCO PNG in collaboration with the Northern Provincial Education Division.

The cultural show was first introduced in 2024 at Afore High School. In 2025, Martyrs Memorial Secondary School hosted the event. This year, 2026, Kokoda Junior High School took the lead.

Speaking at the event, UNESCO PNG Director General, Joseph Auli said the organization has observed positive behavioral changes in students over the three years of funding the program.

“I am impressed to see school children participating in cultural show. UNESCO recognizes culture as important to human development, identity, and peace,” Auli said.

“As we celebrate culture today, we are also shaping our future through preserving both tangible and intangible cultural heritage.”

He elaborated that tangible heritage includes traditional tools, carvings, pottery, clothing, bilums, houses, archaeological sites, sacred places, and museum collections.

While intangible heritage includes indigenous languages, oral traditions, songs, dance, customs, and ceremonies.

Auli urged students to take an active role in preserving their culture:

“You are not just the future custodians of PNG’s cultural heritage, but the future of our culture going forward. You can start building this future today through learning traditional stories, mastering traditional songs and dances, documenting community history, and using technology to preserve and promote our heritage globally.” Auli said.

The participating schools were Kokoda Junior High, Kokoda Primary, Mamba Primary, Kiorota Primary, Ioma Junior High, Martyrs Secondary, and Tufi Junior High School.

Kiorota Primary and Ioma Junior High School will co-host the next Provincial Schools Cultural Show in 2027.

item.content:encoded:
‎The difficulty in disseminating important health information to rural health facilities in Milne Bay has greatly affected the progress of health services in the Milne Provincial Health Authority (MBPHA). ‎ ‎The launch of its new website and intranet system is expected to greatly improve its information sharing between the Provincial health authority, its health facilities in the rural areas and the general public. ‎ ‎The Milne Bay Provincial Health Authority (MBPHA), on Wednesday, launched its website and intranet system as a way to improve communication and information sharing across all its health facilities in the province. ‎ ‎The Acting Chief Executive officer, Dr Dale Frank, at the launching said the website and intranet system is very important, especially with information dissemination. ‎ ‎"Many a times people ring us asking for information regarding health services, maybe introduction of new fees to certain services, we can't answer everyone who need that information.

‎"When people understand the health information we provide, they'll understand what it means to their life. We have a lot of issues in the hospital, but we can't go and talk to everybody, the website will. In this age and time, students may want to do assignments on health, the website will assist them in finding out the services we offer." Dr Frank said. ‎ ‎MBPHA Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Manager, Newton Jau, said the newly developed intranet will now enhance fast tracking of information and transform health service delivery across the province. ‎ ‎He added the intranet will now connect the Provincial hospital with patients and the health workers while strengthening access to patients' information, including laboratory results and treatments among other health services. ‎ ‎The MBPHA website will also promote accountability and transparency, it will also provide information to the general public, development partners and donors about the authorities' functions and services. ‎ ‎The website will also provide information about the operations of every health facility throughout Milne Bay Province. ‎

item.title: Ragiampun community in Morobe face water crisis
item.description: Families in Ragiampun village in Umi LLG, Markham District, Morobe province, are walking up to 15 minutes to the Yati River for water after their main community pump stopped working. The pump served Ragiampun and nearby communities for more than 30 years, providing water for drinking, cooking, washing and gardens.
item.content:encoded:
Families in Ragiampun village in Umi LLG, Markham District, Morobe province, are walking up to 15 minutes to the Yati River for water after their main community pump stopped working.

The pump served Ragiampun and nearby communities for more than 30 years, providing water for drinking, cooking, washing and gardens.

Residents are now calling on their local leaders to act, saying the lack of a reliable water supply is putting pressure on families, particularly young people who carry water home.

Ward 12 recorder Charles Edward Nario said the community needs a long-term solution.

He has called on the Ward 12 and Ward 13 councillors, Umi LLG and Markham District authorities to work with residents to provide a water tank and pumping system.

“Clean and reliable water is a basic service,” Nario said.

item.title: New Administration building for UOG
item.description: As the country prepares to celebrate the 51 st Independence, it is another milestone achievement for the country as the Prime Minister opens another state-of-the-art 6 th storey Central Administration and Humilaveka Student Forum building at the University of Goroka. PM Marape when cutting the ribbon said this shows the Government’s commitment to quality education for the future.
item.content:encoded:
As the country prepares to celebrate the 51 st Independence, it is another milestone achievement for the country as the Prime Minister opens another state-of-the-art 6 th storey Central Administration and Humilaveka Student Forum building at the University of Goroka.

PM Marape when cutting the ribbon said this shows the Government’s commitment to quality education for the future.

He said the future of the country depend on the quality of teaching and learning in the classroom and UOG as a teacher training institution must continue to produce more teachers for the country.

He thanked Chaina Railway Company for constructing a modern 6 th storey modern building for the staff and students to use.

Member for Goroka, Aiye Tambua on behalf of the people of Goroka District in which the university is situated thanked the government for investing in education.

Mr. Tambua said he is humbled for such a magnificent building on Humilaveka and appeals to the people to look after this government infrastructure.

The K135m building is funded by the government and includes university offices and student forum and an underground carpark.
